summary.intent: The user drove the CipherBox v2 rewrite through a marathon session spanning dependency audits, parallel implementation of unblocked issues, mandatory review gates, and serially working a CodeRabbit review queue to land ~15 PRs in dependency order while keeping GitHub issue metadata (dependencies, milestones, tracker) accurate and machine-readable.
summary.outcome: Landed a large batch of PRs (#951,#952,#955,#957,#960,#961,#967,#969,#977,#978,#968,#971 merged), caught and fixed multiple semantic merge conflicts that would have broken main (#944/#946, #961 vs #957, #969-related), converted 53 prose dependency edges to native GitHub issue dependencies, ran a #635 delivery audit revealing it was only ~55-60% complete, cleaned up 150+ stale worktrees/branches, and left #979/#980/#982 rebased and verified with #980 still needing a post-#982 integration rework.

repo: CipherBox v2: crates/core (crypto/codec), crates/engine (facade.rs, sync/drain.rs, net/, grants/, rotation/ are hottest shared files touched by many PRs concurrently)

Zeroize discipline: terminal-owner-only wiping; `versions.into_iter().next()` is a ptr::read that skips Drop on slot 0 — must use `.first().cloned()` to keep Vec owning its elements so in-place drop zeroizes
Encode/decode fail-closed symmetry: decode-side hard rejects require release-active encode-side Err, never debug_assert!
GitHub native issue dependencies API: POST /repos/{o}/{r}/issues/{n}/dependencies/blocked_by requires issue_id (database id, not issue number) and auto-reciprocates into the upstream's `blocking`
CodeRabbit edits ONE status comment in place per PR — a rebase push overwrites the previous review's content, so reading it after a push cannot reveal what it said before
CodeRabbit skips draft PRs entirely ('Review skipped: draft pull request') so pushing fixes to a draft is free and doesn't burn a review slot

CodeRabbit review budget is ~1/hour org-wide but not strictly periodic; toggling ready then re-draft does NOT cancel an in-flight review (proven via #950 timeline: ready→draft 12s apart, review posted 7min later)
packages/client/vitest.config.ts scopes vitest to src/**/*.test.ts only — test/browser/*.spec.ts (Playwright) is never run by `pnpm -r run test`, a silent gate gap that bit multiple review agents

apps/api test tiers are glob-driven across 3 vitest configs (unit/.test.ts, integration/.integration.test.ts, scheduled/.scheduled.test.ts) — renaming test files risks silently dropping suites from CI

RETIRE_BATCH_MAX → REGISTRY_BATCH_MAX move (#946): a deleted const conflicts loudly in git but a new importer of the old name auto-merges silently into E0432 — same class as PreservedFields Vec::new() sites and folderName field additions on SnapshotView
test/browser/build-wasm.mjs hardcodes <repo>/target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/debug path and ignores CARGO_TARGET_DIR — must run browser suite with `env -u CARGO_TARGET_DIR`

target-*/ scratch dirs (worktree-local CARGO_TARGET_DIR convention) were untracked but NOT covered by .gitignore's `target/` entry, and eslint.config also only ignored `target/**` not `target-*/` — fixed both in a chore PR
Squash merges mean `git branch --merged`/`git cherry` cannot detect merged feature branches — must query PR state via gh api instead

GitHub PR mergeable=true / green CI says nothing about a pairwise merge with another PR — must build the actual merge and run gates; caught 4+ instances of this class (#944/#946, #961 vs #957, #955/#957 vs stale main)

code.finding: open_content_range's assembly buffer was a bare Vec, stranding plaintext unwiped on both trust-rejection error paths and on every reallocation past prealloc budget; fixed with Zeroizing<Vec<u8>> + mem::take on success, and a grow_wiping() helper that wipes the outgrown allocation before Vec growth

versions.into_iter().next() was a ptr::read bitwise move that let IntoIter::drop skip zeroizing slot 0's SecretBytes content key; regression vs main's borrow-based versions.first(); fixed via .first().cloned()

rebase_create and rebase_update_content both test working.contains(op.target) but reach opposite conclusions (Dropped vs replays) — for UpdateContent this is ambiguous between a genuine concurrent edit and a self-replay, letting a crashed-and-replayed op unpin already-published content via a stale UploadCancels session-scoped interlock (#966)

an_owning_guard_wipes_the_tree_it_took only asserted pre-drop readability, never post-drop wipe state, making it vacuous; CodeRabbit's proposed fix called zeroize_bytes() manually which tests that function not ScrubOwned::drop; fixed by making ScrubOwned<T:Scrub> generic with Drop calling self.0.scrub(), verified red-before-green by gutting Drop

portFor's newest-wins fallback answered ticket requests from the wrong tab's port registry when no own port existed for a clientId, causing mid-playback 404s after SW restart; restricted fallback to ANONYMOUS_CLIENT only

concurrent_raises_never_regress_a_floor lock necessity verified empirically: 0/40 pass with write_lock removed, 40/40 with it present — CodeRabbit's determinism nitpick was declined since making it deterministic via a test-only hook would weaken what the test proves

workflow: Verify agent-reported claims independently before relaying to the user — caught an agent fabricating a CodeRabbit review quote (#969) and a report that Vec::new() at contract.rs:1178 would break #961's merge with main

Mutation-test security/coverage fixes: revert the fix, confirm the new test fails with the expected error signature, then restore — used repeatedly to catch circular or vacuous tests (zeroize watchdog, floor_store lock, media range coverage)

When N PRs share hot files, dispatch rebase+verify agents in parallel only if their touched-file sets are disjoint; otherwise extend the existing agent's brief via SendMessage rather than spawning a second agent on the same worktree

Build the actual pairwise/N-way merge and run real gates before trusting 'MERGEABLE + green CI' on a stale PR — this is the only reliable check for semantic (type-level) conflicts that git's conflict detection misses entirely

Bash loops that reassign PATH or use zsh's special `path` array clobber the environment silently, causing every subsequent command in the loop to fail with misleading 'not found' errors — always use unique variable names and absolute binary paths in monitor/loop scripts

Guard-then-write patterns must gate the actual mutating call (PATCH/upload), not just the local transform — a `test -s` check on a 1-byte fetched file can pass while the fetch itself silently failed, letting a bad PATCH through anyway
CodeRabbit's cited 'coding guideline' text should be grep-verified against the repo's actual docs before accepting a finding — fabricated citations occurred at least 3 times this session

friction: Repeated pairwise/semantic merge conflicts (#944/#946 RETIRE_BATCH_MAX, #961 vs #957 PreservedFields, multiple 'stale base = false green CI' cases) required manual merge-building since neither git nor CI catches them

CodeRabbit review timing is unpredictable (~1/hr, not strictly periodic) causing wasted toggle windows (#946 got zero review after a 2-min window, #961 got zero review after both a 2-min and a 10-min window)
gh pr ready call failures were silently swallowed by /dev/null redirection in early monitor scripts, producing a false 'rate-limited' diagnosis instead of surfacing the real gh error
CodeRabbit overwrites its own status comment in place on every push, destroying the record of prior review outcomes — led to briefly misreporting #969 as never-reviewed

Transient GitHub API network errors (`dial tcp ... connection refused`) needed distinguishing from 'no review yet' in polling loops; an earlier loose string match (`*20*`) could have misread a network error as a landed review timestamp
AskUserQuestion / multiple-choice prompts are broken on the user's mobile client (appear then disappear before readable) — required switching to plain text throughout the session
No tsconfig covers packages/client/test/browser, so drifted test doubles (missing methods) can compile silently — discovered via #951's StubEngineHost consolidation (led to issue #975)
open_items: #980 needs a full integration rewrite of its leader-relay/stream layer after #982 lands (5 files, 10 conflicting hunks, competing redesigns of downloadRange vs openContentStream/readStream/closeStream)
#982's pushChunk write path still broadcasts plaintext over BroadcastChannel — deliberately deferred as issue #983

#954/#635-adjacent grant delivery and #635 itself: audit showed #635 is only ~55-60% delivered (write revoke/downgrade and invites are 0%), scope needs restating and the #784/#953 edges need correction — not yet applied
#973: crypto-privacy-review.md command file still specifies v1 primitives (AES-GCM/ECIES/TEE) instead of v2 (XChaCha20-Poly1305/BLAKE3/X25519+HPKE) — filed but not fixed
#970: VITE_WEB3AUTH_VERIFIER repo variable unset, blocking staging login verification and #888/#809/#653
#975: no tsconfig for packages/client/test/browser — filed, not started
155 branches with no PR left untouched intentionally (v1, backups, research/* refs)
gitignore/eslint target-*/ fix committed to a new chore branch but PR not yet opened/pushed at transcript end
